parallel.requirements: Recognized a clean-room reverse-engineering task for the ngrrram TUI: observe the binary and documentation only, do not decompile or wrap, and produce an original executable.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation on its own todo list but delegated eight independent data-extraction ranges to swarm children after building common helper scripts.
parallel.implementation: Produced harness.py, vt.py, driver.py, frames.py, extract.py, captures, logs, and JSON datasets; no replacement source tree or compileable executable was created.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No integration phase occurred. Child extraction outputs and the shared helper patch were not assembled into the required final executable before cancellation.
parallel.verification: Verified selected probe behavior and child JSON extraction outputs, but never ran acceptance tests against a replacement implementation because none existed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run ended by cancellation after continued UI probing; the artifact was not a compileable reimplementation and official evaluation failed compile_failed with 332 tests not run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering constraints and focused on reproducing the TUI behavior from documentation and PTY observations.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all work in the main agent: build VT tooling, probe CLI and TUI behavior, then reimplement in pure Rust and diff-test.
serial.implementation: Created probe/drive.py, probe/term.py, and a temporary Rust TUI test attempt, then gathered behavior details; no final replacement implementation was written.
serial.integration_and_delivery: There were no delegated components to integrate and no final executable assembly beyond packaging the workspace as-is.
serial.verification: Performed local observational probes for typing, CLI validation, keyboard display, layout variants, empty wordlist panic, and frame rate, but no evaluator-aligned final verification.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run was cancelled while still investigating; the submitted artifact contained probes rather than a compileable clone and failed compile_failed with 332 tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run understood the clean-room task and investigated CLI/TUI behavior and embedded n-gram lists without forbidden source inspection.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run understood the same clean-room task and used local PTY observation to inspect CLI/TUI behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference explains the outcome; both knew they needed an original replacement but neither delivered one.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent planned UI probing, data extraction, implementation, and verification, then delegated eight extraction slices to subagents while retaining implementation locally.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial attempt made the same stages local work, with no subagents and a todo list ending in pure-std Rust implementation and diff testing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used decomposition only for data extraction; serial kept a single owner. Neither established a completed implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Children received exact extractor commands and validation instructions, but the parent got an aggregate completion result that mixed true completion with children that had only launched detached work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child interfaces; it kept observations and probe code in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel interface problem was a result-lifecycle handoff after the swarm, not a missing child brief; serial avoided that boundary entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built analysis helpers and an extractor, then continued probing details such as layout, cat animation, error display, and special keys.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built probe scripts and gathered detailed byte-level behavior including lesson completion, CLI errors, keyboard layout, and frame rate.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel accumulated more extracted n-gram data through children; serial developed more local byte-level observations. Both stopped before writing the clone.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The AgentSwarm aggregate returned completed while several subagents had only launched background tasks; the parent saw no tracked tasks and partial output files, then continued independent probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial probes returned directly in the main trajectory, so there was no child completion, retrieval, or join lifecycle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an adverse child result lifecycle; serial's failure was not caused by a delegated result being dropped.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A child edited the shared driver.py helper to fix an fd leak, but the shared write did not produce a proven collision or final deliverable overwrite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote local probe files under probe/ and had no concurrent shared workspace writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more shared-state surface, but the only concrete shared edit was a helper fix; the missing final executable came from lack of integration and closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified some child JSON extraction outputs and UI probes, but never verified a replacement executable; official evaluation completed with compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified observed behaviors with local probes but likewise had no final executable to validate; official evaluation completed with compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Verification differed in local versus delegated observations, but both lacked whole-task acceptance against a delivered implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 109 tool calls and eight subagents, timed out, and its main trajectory was cancelled during additional probing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 39 tool calls with no subagents, also timed out, and was cancelled during a frame-rate probe follow-up.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra budget coordinating extraction work, while serial spent its budget on local probes; both crossed the deadline without implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both modes failed with compile_failed and no tests ran. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level: parallel delegated n-gram extraction and mishandled the returned/detached child work, while serial kept probing local. Neither mode converted observations into a compileable replacement executable.
parallel_contributors: Delegated extraction outputs and child reports were not joined into an implementation path after the swarm aggregate returned.
The parent continued probing UI details until cancellation rather than building and packaging the replacement executable.
serial_contributors: The serial run also remained in exploratory probing and was cancelled before implementation.
The serial artifact contained probe code and no compileable replacement executable.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel recovered more n-gram datasets through children, including a child-side fd-leak fix, while serial focused on byte-level rendering and timing details.
Because both runs lacked a final implementation, the official evaluator stopped at compile_failed rather than exposing behavioral score differences.
evaluator_effects: Both official evaluator summaries report compile_failed with 332 tests not run, so the evaluator did not distinguish the partial behavioral observations.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a realized adverse parallel process issue, not a cause of a discordant score

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly kept implementation as a planned task; the failure was that it never reached that work, not that no implementer was assigned.
No separately implemented components were produced that needed interface reconciliation into a coherent program.
There was no complete candidate implementation ready for entry-point placement or packaging; final assembly was not the first missing owner.
The workflow did not have owned implementation/build/test stages whose handoff was unowned; the parent retained the end-to-end plan but stayed in investigation.
No single mandatory preflight gate blocked all productive work; the parent both probed and delegated extraction in parallel.
Although implementation was deferred, the parallel episode was not a completed investigation phase; the direct problem was unmanaged child results and detached extraction work.
Implementation was late, but the evidence points to parent-owned investigation and result lifecycle failure rather than workers being concentrated away from a known critical implementation path.
Eight extraction children increased budget use, but the retained boundary is that the returned and file-visible results were not actively joined; fan-out alone is not sufficient.
Each child had one bounded extraction slice and most completed or retried successfully; no single overbroad child assignment left indispensable implementation work unfinished.
The child briefs gave exact commands, output names, validation steps, and crash-retry instructions for the extraction-only task.
The delegated outputs were separate JSON/log files with deterministic names; no incompatible independently owned components needed an omitted interoperability contract.
No known requirement or finding is shown disappearing through summarization or transfer; the problematic results were available or file-visible rather than lost in transfer.
Child reports were concise status summaries and JSON files; there is no evidence the parent was unable to reduce an oversized handoff.
No parent action relied on a handoff that described a superseded workspace or requirement state.
The child outputs did not present incompatible contracts or reports that the parent failed to adjudicate.
The parent never presented the whole task as complete; the run ended by cancellation before any final acceptance decision.
The observed retry after the tetra4 extraction crash carried a diagnosis and changed driver.py to close the fd, so it was not checkpoint-free repeated work.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No parent action explicitly stopped or cancelled an active child before its needed result; the run-level cancellation occurred after continued parent work.
No complete replacement implementation or mutually compatible component set was ready to promote; only probes and extraction artifacts existed.
No implementation result was merged after an integrated verification step, and there was no final replacement to verify.
The children were delegated extraction tasks, not implementation tasks; no completed child implementation was left unjoined.
No verifier child produced a concrete trapped finding; the relevant outputs were extraction results visible in the aggregate or workspace.
The one clear child failure was diagnosed inside that child, driver.py was patched, and the child retried to successful extraction.

The parent launched eight extraction children, received an aggregate completion report that already contained a concrete completed child report and several background-only pseudo-results, then saw no tracked background tasks while output files and OS extract.py processes still showed incomplete lifecycle state. It moved on with independent probing and never joined the extraction outputs into an implementation.
candidates.realized_consequence: The extracted child work remained outside an implementation path; the parent continued probing until cancellation and submitted no compileable replacement.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent did inspect task and file state instead of only waiting. The concrete error is unconsumed completed or file-visible child work after the swarm returned.

candidates.reason: The parent did not wait passively; it checked TaskList, listed output files, saw extract.py processes, and continued probing.
No concurrent agents wrote competing files that claimed overlapping implementation or build ownership.
A child edited shared driver.py, but there is no observed simultaneous edit conflict or reconciliation of another live writer's change.
No child wholesale replaced or deleted source owned by another actor; the observed helper edit was a targeted fd-leak fix.
No required executable or entry-point source was overwritten by another live actor.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing another actor's final-tree outputs.
Multiple children wrote shared output files, but the filenames were partitioned and no unstable-state or provenance problem beyond the retained result lifecycle was proven.
The JSON extraction artifacts were intended intermediate outputs, not leaked files that another actor consumed as a false reference or stable environment.

retained_patterns.reason: After spawning eight extraction workers, the parent received a completed swarm aggregate but several children had only launched detached work, while at least one actual extraction report was already returned. The parent then found no tracked background tasks, saw zero-byte outputs with eight extract.py processes still running, and continued unrelated probing rather than joining or rejecting the child work.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: The extracted child work remained outside an implementation path; the parent continued probing until cancellation and submitted no compileable replacement.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The parent did inspect task and file state instead of only waiting. The concrete error is unconsumed completed or file-visible child work after the swarm returned.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Blind Timeout Wait was suppressed because the parent inspected state and the same chain is better captured as unused child results.
Fan-out Budget Exhaustion was suppressed because high fan-out and timeout were downstream symptoms without a separate allocation consequence.
Missing Verifier Return was suppressed because the children were extractors, not verifier agents, and the relevant results were visible or file-backed.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; the only retained pattern with direct parallel evidence is the unmanaged returned extraction result episode.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No extra load, finalization, failure-takeover, or write labels were retained because they describe the same timeout chain or lack distinct adverse evidence.
